acts.23.p1.b1.text: Paul looked directly at the Sanhedrin

acts.23.p1.b2.text: “Brothers, I have conducted myself before God in all good conscience to this day.”

acts.23.p1.b3.text: At this, the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.

acts.23.p2.b4.text: “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit here to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by commanding that I be struck.”

acts.23.p2.b5.text: “How dare you insult the high priest of God!”

acts.23.p2.b6.text: “Brothers,” … “I was not aware that he was the high priest, for it is written: ‘Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.’”

acts.23.p3.b7.text: Then Paul, knowing that some of them were Sadducees and others Pharisees,

acts.23.p3.b8.text: “Brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee. It is because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial.”

acts.23.p3.b9.text: As soon as he had said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided. For the Sadducees say that there is neither a resurrection, nor angels, nor spirits, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.

acts.23.p4.b11.text: “We find nothing wrong with this man. What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”

acts.23.p4.b12.text: The dispute grew so violent that the commander was afraid they would tear Paul to pieces.

acts.23.p4.b13.text: He ordered the soldiers to go down and remove him by force and bring him into the barracks.

acts.23.p5.b15.text: the Lord stood near Paul and said,

acts.23.p5.b17.text: As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so also you must testify in Rome.”

acts.23.p6.b18.text: When daylight came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath

acts.23.p6.b19.text: not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.

acts.23.p6.b20.text: More than forty of them were involved in this plot. They went to the chief priests and elders and said,

acts.23.p6.b21.text: “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul. Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him down to you … We are ready to kill him on the way.”

acts.23.p7.b22.text: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the plot,

acts.23.p7.b23.text: he went into the barracks and told Paul.

acts.23.p7.b24.text: “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”

acts.23.p7.b25.text: “Paul the prisoner sent and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”

acts.23.p8.b26.text: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside, and asked,

acts.23.p8.b27.text: “What do you need to tell me?”

acts.23.p8.b28.text: “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow … Do not let them persuade you, because more than forty men are waiting to ambush him. … they are ready now, awaiting your consent.”

acts.23.p8.b29.text: “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”

acts.23.p9.b30.text: Then he called two of his centurions and said,

acts.23.p9.b31.text: “Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea in the third hour of the night.

acts.23.p9.b32.text: Provide mounts for Paul to take him safely to Governor Felix.”

acts.23.p10.b33.text: And he wrote the following letter:

acts.23.p10.b34.text: Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.

acts.23.p10.b35.text: This man was seized by the Jews, and they were about to kill him when I came with my troops to rescue him. For I had learned that he is a Roman citizen,

acts.23.p10.b36.text: I found that the accusation involved questions about their own law, but there was no charge worthy of death or imprisonment.

acts.23.p10.b37.text: When I was informed that there was a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once. …

acts.23.p11.b38.text: So the soldiers followed their orders and brought Paul by night to Antipatris.

acts.23.p11.b39.text: The next day they returned to the barracks and let the horsemen go on with him.

acts.23.p12.b40.text: When the horsemen arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and presented Paul to him.

acts.23.p12.b41.text: The governor read the letter and asked what province Paul was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,

acts.23.p12.b42.text: “I will hear your case when your accusers arrive.”

acts.23.p12.b43.text: Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod’s Praetorium.
